title: Reactions of Metals with Water and Acids

content.text: Reactions of Metals with Water and Acids
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe reactions of metals with water
Describe reactions of metals with dilute acids
Write balanced equations for these reactions
The reactions of metals with water and acids help us understand and confirm the reactivity series. More reactive metals react more vigorously, producing characteristic observations.
Melts into a ball and floats
Melts into a ball and floats
May catch fire (yellow flame) if held in place
Goes cloudy (calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble)
Very slow reaction with cold water
Few bubbles form over several days
[DIAGRAM: Apparatus for magnesium reacting with steam - showing test tube with magnesium ribbon heated, steam passing over it]
Metals below calcium in the reactivity series react with steam (not cold water):
Reactions of Metals with Dilute Acids
Vigorous fizzing, gets hot, metal disappears quickly
Slow at first, then moderate fizzing (oxide layer)
Slow fizzing, solution turns pale green
Apply a burning splint to the gas
[DIAGRAM: Test tube with metal in acid, collecting gas, burning splint test]
Copper, silver, and gold are below hydrogen in the reactivity series:
They cannot displace hydrogen from acids
They hold onto their electrons too tightly
No reaction occurs with dilute HCl or H₂SO₄
Write a balanced equation for the reaction of calcium with water.
Calcium reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide and hydrogen
Calcium has a 2+ charge, so formula is Ca(OH)₂
Describe what you would see when magnesium ribbon is added to dilute sulfuric acid.
Write a balanced equation for zinc reacting with dilute hydrochloric acid, including state symbols.
Explain why copper does not react with dilute sulfuric acid.
Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series
Copper is less reactive than hydrogen
Copper cannot displace hydrogen from the acid
Saying metals react with cold water when they only react with steam
Only K, Na, Li, Ca react with cold water; others need steam or don't react
Confusing the products - hydroxides from water, salts from acids
Water → hydroxide + H₂; Acid → salt + H₂
Write a balanced equation for the reaction of sodium with water. (2 marks)
Describe what you would observe when a small piece of potassium is added to water. (4 marks)
Write a balanced equation with state symbols for the reaction of magnesium with dilute hydrochloric acid. (2 marks)

A student adds iron filings to dilute sulfuric acid. a) Write a balanced equation for the reaction. (2 marks) b) Describe what the student would observe. (2 marks) c) How could the student test for the gas produced? (2 marks)
Explain, in terms of the reactivity series, why zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid but copper does not. (3 marks)
Compare the reactions of lithium and calcium with water. (4 marks)
The production of bubbles of gas
A compound formed when an acid reacts with a metal or base
The sound made when hydrogen burns in air
More reactive metals react more vigorously
K, Na, Li react vigorously/dangerously with cold water
Ca reacts steadily with cold water
Mg, Zn, Fe react with steam but not cold water
Cu, Ag, Au don't react with water or dilute acids
